name: Pete Rock
hook: Learned on Marley Marl's radio show and an SP-1200 he was given, and made the soft, horn-heavy sampled sound that defined early-90s New York.
blurb: Peter Phillips grew up in Mount Vernon, just north of New York City. As a teenager he got a job as a DJ on Marley Marl's radio show on WBLS, 'In Control with Marley Marl', through his cousin Heavy D; archived broadcasts from 1989 and 1990 feature him. The rapper Freddie Foxx gave him an SP-1200 at seventeen, as he has described, and he taught himself to make beats on it. With the rapper CL Smooth he made 'They Reminisce Over You (T.R.O.Y.)' in 1992, written after their friend Troy Dixon, a dancer with Heavy D, died in an accident. Its saxophone line comes from a jazz record by Tom Scott. His early-1990s productions, built from jazz and soul horns, filtered basslines and dense drums, defined a warmer kind of New York hip-hop than the Bomb Squad's noise or Marley Marl's hard loops. He was also a formative influence on J Dilla.
